analyzed_vuln.description: Heap OOB read during GC is caused by integer truncation in SplFixedArray GC metadata. spl_fixedarray_object_get_gc() stores intern->array.size into an int (*n = (int)intern->array.size). For very large SplFixedArray sizes (e.g. 010001000 octal => 2^24), this can overflow to a negative len. gc_mark_grey() then uses uint32_t n = len, turning that negative value into a huge unsigned count and iterating far past the valid zval table, triggering zval_get_type() OOB reads. The crashing site is zend_gc.c:gc_mark_grey/zend_types.h:zval_get_type, but root cause is the bad size contract from SplFixedArray handlers.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: PoV creates a very large SplFixedArray and calls var_dump(), which invokes object property/debug traversal and later GC at request shutdown. Data flow: script -> SplFixedArray(size) in ext/spl -> get_gc() returns table pointer + truncated int len -> zend_gc_collect_cycles()->gc_mark_grey() trusts len and scans zvals with unsigned loop bound. Trigger requires size large enough that (int)size becomes negative (or otherwise invalid), causing massive out-of-bounds traversal.
